newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -CALLS SOLD IN BSKYB AHEAD OF RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -CALLS SOLD IN BSKYB AHEAD OF RESULTS.

text.p: UK equity options traded quietly on Monday despite inherent strength in the stock market as it clawed back early losses, dealers said.

"Part of the reason is that traders think current options prices are too expensive -- owing to increased volatility -- and that the spread (between bid and offer prices) is too wide and therefore won't trade," said one dealer.

Despite such pricing difficulties, there was a seller of 750 September 550 calls at about 6p in satellite television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting ahead of full year results by the company on Friday.

Over in electricals group General Electric Co, the main trade was a long strangle established by buying 405 November 390 puts at 18-1/2p as well as 405 November 420 calls at 12p. Greater implied volatility in GEC shares will help make a profit.
By 1320 GMT, BSkyB shares were up 14-1/2p to 487-1/2p while GEC was down 5-1/2p to 393p.
Traders also showed interest in British Telecommunications where there were buyers of August 425 puts at around 49p and November 385 puts at about 25p.
There were also sellers of November puts which dealers believed were from traders who had bought put options last week and who were now creating put spreads in order to limit risk.

BT shares went ex-dividend on Monday and some options traders may have been attracted by this as well as the uncertainty surrounding BT's plans to merge with MCI Corporation in America. Press reports have suggested that BT may launch a six billion stg buyback if the merger fails.
BT shares fell 44-1/2p to 382p mainly owing to its ex-dividend status.
